newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares close higher as A stocks fall.
newsitem.headline: China B shares close higher as A stocks fall.

text.p: China's foreign currency B shares ended up on Wednesday while domestic A shares fell in slow and choppy trading with investors edgy about aftershocks from government policies to cool the markets, brokers said.
The Shanghai foreign currency B index rose 0.869 points, or 1.01 percent, to 86.632 points on volume of 12.4 million shares worth $9.8 million, compared with $11.711 million on Tuesday.
The Shenzhen B index edged up 0.27 points, or 0.18 percent, to 151.34 on turnover of HK$126.9 million against Tuesday's HK$144.4 million.
"Institutional buying supported the (Shanghai) market today," said one broker. "But volume has not picked up, indicating sentiment is still cautious and the potential for further rises is limited."
Analysts in Shenzhen said B share investors were encouraged by the Hong Kong stock market hitting a record intra-day high but depressed by weak local A shares.
"The Shenzhen B index was caught between its A shares and the Hong Kong index," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

Hong Kong stocks closed the Wednesday morning session at an all-time high with the Hang Seng Index at 14,685.52, riding on renewed red-chip fever -- Hong Kong-listed shares with China backing, brokers said.
The index retreated to close 16.32 points higher at 14,556.48.
But the Shenzhen A index slid 3.64 points, or 0.83 percent, to 436.84 on turnover of 6.5 billion yuan, compared with Tuesday's 6.9 billion.
"The A share investors are largely focused on possible further crackdown measures by Beijing," an analyst at a major Western investment bank said.
State media said on Wednesday the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) had set up two special phone lines for investors to report irregularities and illegal trading on the stock markets.
"People see the phone lines as a warning against stock speculation," the bank analyst said.
Beijing began to implement policies to dampen stock speculation at the start of May, by which time the A and B indices had surged more than 50 percent from the beginning of 1997.
Weifu Fuel Injection Co Ltd was the best performer in the Shenzhen B share market, adding HK$0.34, or 6.77 percent, to HK$5.36.
Shanghai Steel Tube Co was the star in the Shanghai B share market on speculative buying, jumping $0.012, or 7.69 percent, to $0.168 on volume of 20,000 shares.

Blue-chip Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Co was the most actively traded and became the third winner on institutional window-dressing buying, rising $0.042, or 4.66 percent, to $0.942 on volume of 1.7 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index fell 12.615 points, or 0.94 percent, to 1,326.035 points on volume of 449.7 million shares worth seven billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index shed 28.850 points, or 0.73 percent, to 3,939.655.
